jobs.title: Senior Director, Capital Markets Finance
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You’ll Be Doing

As Senior Director, Capital Markets Finance, you will report to and act as a senior advisor the Capital Markets CFO, supporting the broader CFO mandate across financial performance, strategic planning, resource allocation, decision support and transformation. You will bring together strong financial and Capital Markets expertise with a technology and innovation mindset to improve how Capital Markets Finance operates, generates insights and supports business decisions.

A key part of the mandate will be to modernize and automate financial reporting and analytical processes across the Capital Markets CFO teams, identify high-value AI and technology use cases, and lead their implementation in partnership with Finance, Technology and the business. You will remain closely connected to developments in financial markets and the external environment, proactively identifying emerging risks, opportunities and implications for Capital Markets performance and strategy.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview.

How You’ll Succeed

Financial Performance and Insights – Consolidate information across Capital Markets LOBs to provide a holistic view of performance, risk and opportunities. Provide forward-looking analysis across revenue, expenses, balance sheet, capital, liquidity, RWA and other key financial resources. Connect financial results, business drivers and market developments to identify trends, opportunities and emerging risks and provide actionable insights to senior management.
Planning and Forecasting – Lead the consolidation of LOB forecasts and plans, ensuring they are reasonable, aligned with Capital Markets strategy and positioned to deliver key financial and performance objectives. Challenge key business, market and regulatory assumptions and support effective resource allocation and execution.
Finance Transformation, Technology & AI - Lead the modernization of Capital Markets Finance by identifying opportunities to simplify, standardize and automate reporting, forecasting and analytical processes. Identify and lead high-value AI, data and technology use cases from concept through implementation, adoption and measurable outcomes.
Markets Insight - Maintain a strong understanding of financial markets, macroeconomic developments, client activity, competitive dynamics and emerging industry trends. Translate external developments into implications for Capital Markets performance, risks, opportunities and strategic priorities.
Leadership and Governance - Maintain strong financial governance and controls while leading and developing a high-performing Finance team. Set clear priorities, build capabilities, foster collaboration and create an environment of accountability, innovation and continuous improvement.

Who You Are

You act like an owner. You thrive when you're empowered to take the lead, go above and beyond, and deliver results.
You're passionate about people. You find meaning in relationships, and surround yourself with a diverse network of partners. You build trust through respect and authenticity
You're driven by collective success. You know that collaboration can transform a good idea into a great one. You understand the power of an inclusive team that enjoys working together to bring a shared vision to life.
You give meaning to data. You enjoy investigating complex problems, and making sense of information. You're confident in your ability to communicate detailed information in an impactful way.
You can demonstrate a minimum of 5 years working experience in a Finance leadership role, have a professional accounting designation and/or a post graduate business degree, along with good financial accounting knowledge and the ability to comprehend complex accounting issues and summarize them for the business. You also have strong problem solving, analytical, judgment and change implementation capabilities. In addition, you are equally comfortable with Finance and technology. You understand complex financial concepts but also have the curiosity and technical fluency to challenge how work is done and identify where automation, data and AI can fundamentally improve it.
You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.

jobs.title: Director, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A)
jobs.description:
With millions of diners, 70,000+ restaurant partners and 25+ years of experience, OpenTable, part of Booking Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: BKNG), is an industry leader with a passion for helping restaurants thrive. Our world-class technology empowers restaurants to focus on what matters most – their team, their guests, and their bottom line – while enabling diners to discover and book the perfect restaurant for every occasion.

Every employee at OpenTable has a tangible impact on what we do and how we do it. You’ll also be part of a global team and its portfolio of metasearch brands. Hospitality is all about taking care of others, and it defines our culture.

About The Job

OpenTable is seeking a strategic and operationally-minded Director of FP&A to lead financial planning, forecasting, and analysis for our core operational investments. Located in our Toronto office, this role will have primary ownership over the company’s Operating Expenses (OpEx), Capital Expenditures (CapEx), and Commissions modeling and structures. Reporting to the VP, FP&A, you will act as a key business partner to departmental heads, ensuring disciplined resource allocation, optimization of capital investments, and the implementation of commission plans that align with corporate growth objectives. This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Responsibilities

OpEx Management & Forecasting: Lead the annual budgeting and monthly forecasting processes for global operating expenses. Partner with department heads ( tech, sales, marketing, G&A) to track spend, analyze variances, and identify cost-efficiency opportunities.
CapEx Planning & Governance: Oversee the evaluation, tracking, and prioritization of capital expenditures. Develop robust ROI models for major technology, infrastructure, and facilities investments to guide executive decision-making.
Commissions Oversight: Own the financial oversight of the commission program. Partner with Sales Operations to ensure commission plans are accurate and effective.
Business Partnership: Serve as a trusted financial advisor to operational leadership, translating complex financial data into actionable insights that drive strategic initiatives.
Management Reporting: Deliver clear monthly and quarterly financial review packages focusing on spend efficiency, capital deployment, and incentive plan effectiveness for senior leadership.
Process & Systems Improvement: Continuously scale and automate FP&A processes, particularly around expense tracking and commission calculations, to support organizational growth.

Qualifications

Experience: 7–10 years of progressive experience in corporate finance, FP&A, or strategic finance, with a strong emphasis on expense management, capital budgeting, and sales compensation finance.
Leadership: Demonstrated experience managing professional finance team members and leading cross-functional projects.
Analytical Skills: Advanced financial modeling skills (Excel/Google Sheets) and experience handling large datasets. Proficiency with financial planning tools, ERP software, and commission management platforms (e.g., CaptivateIQ).
Communication: Strong ability to influence and build partnerships with non-finance executives by presenting financial concepts clearly and concisely.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related quantitative field.

Benefits and Perks

Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year
Focus on mental health and well-being:
Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth
Company-paid subscription to Headspace
Annual company-wide week off a year - the whole team fully recharges (and returns without a pile-up of work!)

Paid parental leave
Generous paid vacation + time off for your birthday
Paid volunteer time
Focus on your career growth:
Development Dollars
Leadership development
Access to thousands of on-demand e-learnings

Travel Discounts
Employee Resource Groups
20 days of paid time off
Private health and dental insurance
Life and Disability insurance

The best connections happen face-to-face, whether you’re sitting down to dinner or having coffee with a coworker. That’s why OpenTable has adopted a hybrid workplace model. This role aligns with that approach, with an expectation of coming into the office two days a week—giving employees the best of both worlds: in-person collaboration and flexibility.

We offer a competitive base salary and benefits including: health benefits; flexible spending account; retirement benefits; life insurance; paid time off (including PTO, paid sick leave, medical leave, bereavement leave, floating holidays and paid holidays); and parental leave benefits. This role is eligible to be considered for an annual bonus and equity grant.

Work Environment & Flexibility

At OpenTable, we pride ourselves on fostering a global and dynamic work environment. As a team member with us, you will benefit from a schedule tailored to accommodate a global workforce operating across multiple time zones. While the majority of your responsibilities may align with conventional business hours, there will be instances where you are expected to manage communications - via calls, Slack messages, or emails - outside of regular working hours to effectively collaborate with international colleagues, respond to restaurant partners, and/or address urgent matters. OpenTable will always abide by and consider local laws and regulations.

Inclusion

We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels they belong and can thrive. We know the best ideas come when we bring different voices to the table, so we're building a team as dynamic as the diners and restaurants we serve—and fostering a culture where everyone feels welcome to be themselves.

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.

Business Partnering

Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.

jobs.description:
University Hospital Foundation

The University Hospital Foundation is dedicated to a powerful, singular purpose: to continuously seek, inspire and support bold solutions to seemingly insurmountable challenges and ignite new discoveries in health. Responsible for raising and managing funds to advance innovation in prevention, research and patient care, the Foundation strives to transform and redefine health in the Edmonton area, throughout Alberta and around the world so everyone can live a longer, healthier life.

In the past ten years, generous donations from individuals and our corporate and strategic partners have contributed nearly $220 million to advance world-leading patient care at the University of Alberta Hospital, Mazankowski Alberta Heart Institute, and Kaye Edmonton Clinic, as well as groundbreaking research at the University of Alberta.

As an outcome-focused organization, UHF offers a flexible hybrid working environment. To learn more about the University Hospital Foundation, visit www.GiveToUHF.ca and if you have a keen interest in being a part of the future of healthcare in Alberta, please consider applying today!

The Opportunity

As a key member of the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and reporting to the President & CEO, the Chief Catalyst, Enabling Systems and Chief Financial Officer. plays a critical role in developing and implementing the business and financial strategy and enabling systems strategy of the University Hospital Foundation (the Foundation). This position is integral to organizational success in support of the mission, vision, values, and goals of the Foundation.

This role serves as a critical advisor to the President & CEO, the Executive Leadership team and support to the Board of Trustees including their supporting committees.

This role leads the Finance, People & Technology Portfolio and manages a diverse department of professionals who are passionate about contributing to the Foundation’s mission through providing the most efficient and effective operational support. This role is a pivotal member of the leadership team that embraces change as an opportunity to learn and is constantly looking for ways to improve the level of service to internal and external customers.

Key accountabilities include financial and operational activities in the areas of finance & investments, accountability of funded projects, donation services, fund management and distributions, information technology & management, people practices, legal & risk management, and facilities & property management.

Key Responsibilities

The responsibilities of this role include, but are not limited to:

Provide strategic management and oversight to the People, Finance and Technology teams to align with UHF’s long-term strategy to support multiple stakeholders including donors and funding recipients.
Lead financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, audit, compliance, investment oversight, and stewardship of donor funds.
Support the President & CEO, Executive Leadership Team, and Board committees with clear, timely, and strategic advice.
Champion innovation and continuous improvement by modernizing systems, strengthening operational capacity, and encouraging new ways of working.
Advance the Foundation’s technology strategy and roadmap, using technology to improve processes, productivity, decision-making, and organizational scalability.
Ensure strong governance, risk management, legal, privacy, procurement, and compliance practices.
Build and lead a collaborative, customer-centric team that provides excellent service to internal and external stakeholders.
Foster trusted relationships with donors, partners, board members, auditors, investment managers, government representatives, and health-system stakeholders.
Contribute to a culture that is accountable, courageous, innovative, collaborative, and focused on measurable impact.

Qualifications and Experience

The ideal candidate is an innovative, experienced executive financial and operational leader with the ability to translate strategy into effective systems, structures, and results.

They will bring a strong track record in financial stewardship, people leadership, technology-enabled transformation, risk management, and organizational capacity building. Experience in a complex not-for-profit, charitable, healthcare, post-secondary, public-sector, or similarly mission-driven environment would be considered an asset.

Education & Experience

Preferred qualifications include:

A professional accounting designation, such as CPA, or equivalent senior financial leadership experience.
A post-secondary degree in business, finance, human resources, or a related discipline; an MBA or relevant graduate degree would be an asset.
Significant senior financial leadership experience, including experience in a CFO or comparable executive role.
Proven experience leading teams through growth, change, transformation, or modernization.
Strong knowledge of financial planning, investment oversight, fund accounting, reporting, compliance, and risk management.
Experience working with a Board of Directors or Board of Trustees and supporting board-level committees.
Demonstrated expertise in leveraging data, systems, and technology to drive organizational performance, inform strategic decision-making, and advance enterprise priorities.

Behavioral Competencies and Personal Attributes

The Successful Candidate Will Be

Strategic, financially astute, and future-focused.
Innovative and curious, with a willingness to challenge the status quo and explore better ways to deliver impact.
Collaborative, approachable, and able to build trust across teams, partners, and stakeholders.
A clear communicator who can make complex financial and operational matters understandable to non-financial audiences.
Customer-centric, service-oriented, and committed to supporting both internal teams and external partners.
Courageous, accountable, and comfortable leading through ambiguity and change.
A values-driven leader who operates with integrity, sound judgment, and humility.

Measurements of Success Within the First Year

Success In The First Year Will Include

Building trusted relationships with the Board of Trustees, President & CEO, Executive Leadership Team, direct reports, and key external stakeholders.
Establishing clear priorities, accountabilities, and decision-making practices across the enabling systems portfolio
Strengthening finance, people, technology, and operational systems to support improved service, efficiency, and scalability.
Advancing a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and exceptional customer experience.
Supporting strategic partnerships across the health, life sciences, wellness, philanthropic, and public-sector ecosystems.
Contributing meaningfully to organizational priorities, including leadership development, inclusion, operational excellence, and long-term sustainability.

Department

Monday, November 23, 2026

The opportunity

Are you motivated by the chance to help ensure all young people in Canada can access mental health support and Feel Out Loud? Kids Help Phone (KHP) is Canada’s Unlock The Hope Youth Charity. We’re the first and Canada's only national 24/7, free, confidential, and multilingual e-mental health service for youth and a global leader in innovation for youth and their well-being.

The Senior Director, Data Governance and Management leads Kids Help Phone’s enterprise data strategy, governance, and management functions, ensuring data is governed, protected, and leveraged as a strategic asset. Reporting to the EVP, Technology & Data, this role is accountable for data governance, quality, stewardship, architecture, analytics governance, lifecycle management, responsible data use, and AI readiness.

Working across leadership, clinical services, research, privacy, legal, and operational teams, the Senior Director establishes enterprise standards, drives the evolution of KHP’s Data Operating Model, and strengthens organizational data capabilities. The role provides strategic leadership on data-related risks, opportunities, and investments, ensuring data practices support organizational goals, innovation, service excellence, and the trust of youth seeking support. It’ll take courage, collaboration, innovation, resilience and trust. If you’re interested in transforming e-mental health solutions with KHP, you can explore this opportunity today!

The responsibilities

Enterprise Data Strategy:

Develop and lead KHP’s enterprise data strategy and multi-year roadmap, aligning data, analytics, and AI capabilities with organizational priorities.

Define the vision for data governance, architecture, quality, accessibility, and responsible AI adoption.

Advise senior leadership on emerging trends, opportunities, risks, and investments related to data and AI.

Enterprise Leadership & Decision Authority:

Serve as the organization’s senior leader for data governance and management.

Establish enterprise data standards, accountability frameworks, and governance requirements.

Provide strategic guidance on data-related risks, investments, priorities, and key organizational decisions.

Resolve complex, cross-functional issues related to data ownership, quality, metrics, and reporting.

Data Governance & Operating Model:

Lead and evolve KHP’s Data Operating Model, governance frameworks, and enterprise-wide adoption.

Establish clear roles, responsibilities, and decision-making processes for data governance and stewardship.

Identify and mitigate emerging data, technology, and AI-related risks.

Drive KHP’s data transformation journey, advancing organizational data maturity and governance capabilities.

Data Ownership & Stewardship:

Lead the enterprise data stewardship program across business and service areas.

Define stewardship practices, training, and accountability expectations.

Resolve cross-functional issues related to data ownership, quality, access, lifecycle management, and reporting.

Data Quality, Metrics & Analytics:

Oversee data quality, reporting, business intelligence, and analytics governance.

Establish standards for critical data elements, business definitions, metrics, and reporting consistency.

Advance data and analytics capabilities to support evidence-based decision-making and innovation.

Oversee internal staff and external vendor support for ongoing development, optimization, and maintenance of data infrastructure and pipelines

Data Sources, Lifecycle & Responsible Use:

Define governance requirements for data sourcing, retention, lifecycle management, and responsible use.

Support governance processes for research, data sharing, analytics, AI-enabled initiatives, and regulatory compliance.

Ensure data practices align with privacy, security, legal, and ethical standards.

Governance, Adoption & Organizational Capability:

Chair enterprise data governance and stewardship forums and drive accountability across the organization.

Monitor adoption of governance practices and report on key risks, outcomes, and performance measures.

Lead stakeholder engagement, communications, and training to strengthen enterprise data literacy and capability.

Provide leadership and oversight for data governance programs, priorities, resources, and investments.

The qualifications

Minimum 12 years of progressively senior experience in data governance, data management, analytics, information management or related enterprise data disciplines, including significant experience in senior leadership roles with enterprise-wide accountability. 

Demonstrated leadership experience overseeing complex data, governance or operating-model transformation programs and leading program or project delivery professionals. 

Demonstrated experience designing or operationalizing a data governance framework, stewardship model, decision-rights model or enterprise data standards. 

Strong understanding of data ownership, stewardship, data definitions, data quality, metadata, lineage, lifecycle and metric governance. 

Experience optimizing and modernizing data architecture to enhance reliability, consistency and availability of data to end users. 

Demonstrated experience leading leaders and multidisciplinary teams, including establishing functional strategy, organizational capabilities, performance expectations and succession plans. 

Experience facilitating cross-functional decisions where business, technology, privacy, legal, risk and operational perspectives must be reconciled. 

Experience advising executives and senior governance bodies on complex data strategy, risk, investment and organizational decisions. 

Experience overseeing significant vendor relationships, technology investments and/or enterprise transformation budgets. 

Strong understanding of modern data platforms, cloud data architecture, analytics and BI ecosystems, including platforms such as Power BI and Databricks, and the governance implications of emerging AI capabilities. 

Ability to convert complex governance, risk and technical requirements into practical roles, standards, workflows and decision tools. 

Strong written communication, facilitation, stakeholder management and executive presentation skills. 

Sound judgement when working with sensitive information, ambiguity and competing organizational priorities. 

University degree in data/information management, computer science, information systems, business, engineering, health informatics or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of advanced professional experience and education. Graduate-level education is an asset. 

Preferred / Advantageous

Demonstrated experience operating in complex, highly sensitive or regulated data environments; experience with health, clinical, youth or similarly sensitive data environments strongly preferred. 

Knowledge of Canadian privacy requirements, research governance, Indigenous data governance and responsible AI governance. 

Experience governing enterprise metrics, reporting products, Power BI, cloud data platforms, data catalogues or lineage capabilities. 

Relevant certification or training such as DAMA/CDMP, DCAM, privacy, risk, audit or data management certification. 

Experience establishing a new governance function and transitioning responsibilities from a transformation program into ongoing operations.

Kids Help Phone (KHP) is Canada’s only free, national, 24/7, multilingual and confidential e-mental health service for youth to get help and Feel Out Loud. jobs.description:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance. We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture. As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

Data, analytics and AI are critical to AXIS’s ability to make confident decisions, identify opportunities, improve efficiency and create sustainable competitive advantage. The Head of Applied Science & AI Delivery leads the development, management and evolution of AXIS’s portfolio of reusable applied science and AI capabilities.

Rather than owning delivery for individual business initiatives, this role provides the shared services, models, frameworks, engineering patterns and specialist expertise that enable and support delivery of high-quality business solutions rapidly, safely and consistently. The role is accountable for creating scalable, governed capabilities that can be adopted across multiple value streams, reducing duplication and accelerating value from analytics and AI.

What will you do in this role?

Set the platform vision and roadmap: Define and communicate the strategy, architecture and investment roadmap for reusable data science and AI capabilities, aligned with AXIS’s business priorities, enterprise technology strategy and Data & Analytics operating model.
Build reusable capabilities: Lead the design and development of shared AI services, analytical models, accelerators, agent frameworks, evaluation frameworks, experimentation environments and common solution components that can be adopted across multiple business-aligned solutions.
Enable business-aligned delivery: Partner closely with the Head of Insights & Analytics and value-stream teams to understand recurring needs, translate them into platform priorities and ensure capabilities are practical, discoverable, well documented and easy to adopt.
Lead experimentation and innovation: Create a controlled environment for exploration of emerging analytics, machine learning, generative AI and agentic capabilities. Convert successful experimentation into supported, repeatable enterprise components where there is clear value.
Establish product and platform management: Manage analytics and AI capabilities as products through their full lifecycle, with clear ownership, roadmaps, service expectations, adoption measures, technical health indicators and plans for continuous improvement or retirement.
Lead technical standards and engineering excellence: Establish consistent patterns for development, testing, deployment, integration, monitoring, observability, version control, documentation and reuse. Ensure capabilities are robust, maintainable and designed for enterprise scale.
Drive responsible and governed AI: Partner with Data & AI Governance, Information Risk Management, Legal, Compliance and Technology teams to embed responsible AI, model risk management, security, privacy and regulatory requirements into platform capabilities by design.
Own evaluation and monitoring frameworks: Ensure reusable approaches are in place to evaluate model and agent quality, performance, reliability, safety and value, and to monitor deployed capabilities throughout their lifecycle.
Advance the technology ecosystem: Work closely with Data Platforms & Engineering and Business Technology Solutions to shape and implement the analytics and AI technology stack, integration patterns and deployment pathways across Azure and Databricks.
Build and lead a high-performing specialist team: Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team of data scientists, applied scientists and AI engineers. Set a high bar for technical and academic rigour while fostering collaboration, inclusion, curiosity and pragmatic delivery.
Manage demand, capacity and investment: Prioritise the platform backlog based on enterprise value, reuse potential, risk reduction and strategic fit. Manage resources, budgets, suppliers and delivery commitments transparently.
Champion adoption and reuse: Promote awareness and effective use of shared capabilities, provide technical enablement to delivery teams and actively identify opportunities to consolidate duplicated solutions or patterns

How This Role Works With Insights & Analytics

The Insights & Analytics teams are aligned to business value streams and are accountable for identifying opportunities, defining priorities, designing solutions for each business need, delivering business-aligned solutions and driving adoption and measurable value. The Analytics & AI Platforms team is accountable for the reusable technical capabilities, frameworks, standards and specialist expertise that enable those teams to deliver at greater speed, quality and scale.

Both teams share accountability for successful end-to-end outcomes. The platform team does not become a central delivery queue for every use case, and business-aligned teams should reuse enterprise capabilities wherever practical rather than creating parallel solutions.

Success Measures / Key Outcomes

Reuse and adoption: Shared analytics and AI capabilities are adopted across multiple value streams, with evidence that reuse is reducing duplicated effort and accelerating delivery.
Speed and scalability: Business-aligned teams can move from opportunity to production more quickly because common services, patterns and deployment pathways are available and reliable.
Quality and reliability: Platform capabilities meet agreed standards for performance, availability, maintainability, documentation, monitoring and support.
Responsible delivery: Analytics and AI capabilities operate within AXIS governance, security, privacy, model risk and responsible AI requirements, with effective controls embedded by design.
Business enablement: Capability investments are demonstrably connected to priority business outcomes and enable solutions that are adopted and deliver measurable value.
Technology modernisation: The portfolio evolves in a controlled way to take advantage of relevant advances in data science, machine learning, generative AI and agentic technology.
Team performance: A highly engaged, inclusive and technically strong team with clear accountabilities, effective development pathways and a culture of collaboration and continuous improvement.
Cost and portfolio discipline: Investment is focused on capabilities with enterprise value and reuse potential, with transparent management of cost, technical debt, suppliers and lifecycle decisions.

About You

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table. While there are qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge may help you fulfil this role and contribute to our goals.

What You Need To Have

Platform and product leadership: Significant experience defining and delivering a platform, product or reusable capability strategy in a complex organisation, with accountability for roadmaps, prioritisation, adoption and lifecycle management.
Technical leadership: Deep experience in data science, machine learning and AI, including generative AI, with the credibility to set technical direction, challenge design decisions and lead senior specialists.
Insurance or financial services experience: Understanding of the data, analytical, regulatory and risk context of insurance or another highly regulated industry.
Enterprise AI engineering: Strong understanding of how analytical models and AI services are developed, evaluated, deployed, monitored and operated at scale, including modern software engineering and MLOps or LLMOps practices.
Cloud and data platforms: Strong knowledge of Azure AI services and Azure Databricks, together with practical understanding of enterprise data architectures, APIs, deployment pipelines and integration patterns.
Responsible AI and risk: Experience embedding governance, security, privacy, controls and responsible AI practices into the design and operation of analytics and AI capabilities.
Strategic and commercial judgement: Ability to balance innovation, speed, enterprise value, cost, risk and technical sustainability when making platform investment and prioritisation decisions.
Collaborative operating style: Demonstrated success working across business-aligned analytics teams, engineering, architecture, technology, governance and senior stakeholders to deliver shared outcomes without relying solely on direct authority.
People leadership: Proven ability to build, lead and develop multidisciplinary technical teams and create a high-performance, inclusive and learning-oriented culture.
Communication and influence: Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical concepts, choices and risks clearly to executives, business leaders and delivery teams.
Delivery leadership: Ability to operate in a fast-paced environment, manage multiple priorities and provide clear direction, resource planning, cost oversight and delivery transparency.

What We Prefer You To Have

Relevant technical background: Advanced technical education or equivalent professional experience in data science, computer science, statistics, engineering or a related field.
Enterprise implementation experience: A track record of building reusable analytics or AI platforms and taking generative AI or agentic capabilities from experimentation into governed enterprise use.
Technical depth: Strong working knowledge of Python, Databricks, foundational models, evaluation techniques, retrieval patterns, agent architectures, deployment pipelines and monitoring approaches.

Role Factors

Narvar
is Growing! We're looking for a leader to own the machine learning systems behind post-purchase commerce — identity, fraud, and the intelligence layer that agentic AI runs on.

Hundreds of millions of consumers interact with Narvar every year, across 20B+ orders and 1,300+ retail brands. That data powers three systems: Graphite
, our identity resolution engine that ties fragmented consumer data into a single verified identity across retailers; IRIS
, our fraud and returns-abuse detection engine built on top of it.

You'll own the ML organization behind all of it — the models, the platform they run on, and the people who build them. This is a role for someone who wants a system with real consequences: fraud decisions that move retailer margin, identity resolution that agents make automated decisions on, and an adversary on the other side who adapts every quarter.

For this role, you should be located in Canada and able to work within EST/EDT OR PST hours. We are fully remote.

Day-to-day

Own the ML charter across identity resolution, fraud and abuse detection, risk scoring, and consumer intelligence — strategy, roadmap, and delivery
Build and grow a high-performing, globally distributed team of ML engineers; hire, coach, and develop senior ICs and managers
Set the technical bar for how models get built, evaluated, deployed, and monitored — and hold the org to it
Push identity resolution coverage, precision, and profile classification accuracy against a measured, frozen-holdout baseline — not against vibes
Own IRIS model performance end-to-end: detection rate, false-positive rate, label quality, and the feedback loops that keep both honest as fraud patterns shift
Build the ML platform layer — feature stores, training pipelines, model registry, online serving, drift and performance monitoring — so model velocity isn't bottlenecked on infrastructure
Partner with the AI engineering team so identity and risk signals are first-class inputs to NAVI's agent decisions
Work directly with Product, Engineering, Security, and Customer Success to translate messy retailer problems into ML problems worth solving — and to say no to the ones that aren't
Own build-vs-buy and data-partner decisions (third-party identity data, enrichment providers), including the economics
Communicate model performance, risk, and tradeoffs credibly to executives, retailers, and the board

What We're Looking For

We care more about judgment and ownership
than credentials.

You're Likely a Strong Fit If You

Have 12+ years in engineering with 5+ years managing ML or data teams, including managing managers or senior ICs
Are an engineer at heart — you can still read a training pipeline, review a feature spec, and tell when an eval is measuring the wrong thing
Have shipped ML systems that make consequential automated decisions in production, and have owned them after launch — drift, retraining, incidents, and all
Have deep experience with at least one of: entity resolution / identity graphs, fraud and abuse detection, risk scoring, or anomaly detection at scale
Understand what makes ML different from software: labels are noisy and delayed, systems fail silently, offline metrics lie, and last quarter's model is fighting last quarter's adversary
Have opinions about evaluation — precision/recall tradeoffs on heavily imbalanced data, holdout hygiene, feedback loops where the model's own decisions contaminate future labels
Have built or scaled ML infrastructure: feature pipelines, training orchestration, online model serving with real latency budgets, monitoring and alerting
Are fluent in Python and comfortable in a modern data stack (Spark, Airflow or equivalent, streaming, cloud data warehouses — we run on GCP)
Have hired well, retained well, and can point to engineers whose careers got better on your watch
Excel in a fast-paced environment with a flat structure — you set direction by earning trust, not by mandate
Have a BS/MS in computer science, statistics, or an equivalent background

Bonus points

These Aren't Hard Requirements, But Strong Indicators

You've worked on identity resolution or graph systems against third-party consumer data (credit bureau, telecom, or similar), including the matching logic and confidence scoring underneath
You've operated adversarial ML systems where attackers actively adapt to your detection
You've built real-time inference paths where identity or risk has to be resolved inside a request budget
You've worked in retail, payments, fintech, insurance, or marketplace trust & safety
You've partnered closely with LLM/agent teams and understand how structured ML signals ground agentic decisions
You've navigated privacy, consent, and data-governance constraints on consumer identity data
You've done 0→1 — stood up a function, a platform, or a data partnership from nothing
You use modern tooling (including AI-assisted development workflows) to increase leverage, not outsource thinking

Why ML at Narvar?

Because the data is genuinely rare and the problems are genuinely hard.

The dataset is a moat. Cross-retailer visibility across 20B+ orders means we can see coordinated fraud patterns no single retailer can — a returns abuser hitting five brands looks like a good customer at each one.
The problem is adversarial and unsolved. Returns fraud and policy abuse are growing faster than retail itself, and the counterparty adapts. There is no off-the-shelf answer.
The stakes are measurable. Fraud loss, false-positive cost, identity coverage, resolution rate. Not vanity metrics.
It feeds something bigger. As AI shopping agents enter commerce, every agent will need a trust layer for returns, claims, and delivery promises. Identity and risk are that layer — and you'd own it.
The work is greenfield enough to matter. Real-time resolution, cold-start modeling, historical backfill, new data partnerships — these are decisions still being made, not legacy you inherit.

Why Narvar (from an engineer's perspective)?

Real scale, real customers, real consequences
Startup-level ownership with platform-level impact
Teams that value thinking, judgment, and responsibility
Low ego, high trust, and room to do your best work

We're on a mission to simplify the everyday lives of consumers. Post-purchase is a critical phase of the customer journey. That's why we created Narvar - a platform focused on driving customer loyalty through seamless post-purchase experiences that allow retailers to retain, engage, and delight customers. If you've ever bought something online, there's a good chance you've used our platform!

From the hottest new direct-to-consumer companies to retail’s most renowned brands, Narvar works with GameStop, Neiman Marcus, Sonos, Nike, and 1300+ other brands. With hubs in San Francisco, Atlanta, London, and Bangalore, we've served over 125 million consumers worldwide across 10+ billion interactions, 38 countries, and 55 languages.

Pioneering the post-purchase movement means navigating into the unknown. Our team thrives on this sense of adventure while nurturing a mindset of innovation. We're a home for big hearts and we leave our egos at the door. We work hard but we always make time to celebrate professional wins, baby showers, birthday parties, and everything in between.

new_jobs.title: Director, Technology
new_jobs.description:
The Director, Technology is to ensure that the BC Cancer Foundation has reliable, secure and fit-for-purpose technology services that enable our people to work effectively, strengthen fundraising and donor engagement, and support our 2030 strategic ambitions. The role translates business needs into technology solutions and measurable service improvements, maximizing the value of existing platforms while preparing the Foundation for evolving needs.

Working through a shared-service and vendor-led delivery model, the Director is accountable for dependable technology services, effective provider partnerships, oversight of technology risk. This is a hands-on leadership role: the Director sets the technology roadmap, makes informed trade-offs, resolves issues, delivers improvements and works directly with partners and internal teams to get results.

Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Chief Strategy & Business Intelligence Officer, the Director leads a small team and works closely with business leaders, the Provincial Health Services Authority (PHSA) and technology vendors to ensure technology investments are adopted, secure, cost-effective, and responsive to the Foundation’s priorities.

Key Accountabilities

1. Technology Enablement, Roadmap & Value

Translate BCCF's enterprise technology strategy and organizational priorities into a practical, sequenced roadmap that optimizes existing platforms, enables new capabilities and delivers measurable improvements in productivity, fundraising, donor engagement, and operational effectiveness.
Partner with business leaders to understand pain points and future requirements; identify when to optimize existing tools, improve processes, integrate platforms, or recommend new solutions.
Partner with the data team to ensure a reliable and secure technology platform underpins our reporting and analytics and accessible data and evolving organizational needs.
Evaluate and prioritize technology initiatives based on business value, donor and employee experience, reliability, security, cost, adoption and organizational capacity; define measurable benefits and track results.
Provide technical and commercial advice to enterprise planning, platform decisions, automation and responsible AI adoption, in alignment with enterprise governance.

2. Technology Service Delivery & Operational Excellence

Ensure dependable day-to-day technology services for all our staff. or another vendor.
Lead operational issue resolution and escalation; establish service expectations, reporting, clear ownership and follow-through for incidents, requests, root causes and recurring problems.
Ensure seamless employee onboarding, changes and offboarding, including devices, identity, permissions, licenses, collaboration tools and access to critical business applications.
Continuously improve employee technology experience and operational efficiency through simple processes, fit-for-purpose support, clear documentation and actionable service measures.

3. Strategic Partnerships, Contracts & Service Accountability

Own and strengthen the operational technology partnership with PHSA, defining service scope, accountability, escalation, decision rights, administrative access, and a fit-for-purpose future service model for BCCF.
Manage relationships and performance across key enterprise and SaaS providers, including Blackbaud and other platforms supporting fundraising, finance, and donor engagement.
Negotiate and oversee contracts, service levels, licenses, renewals and vendor roadmaps; hold partners accountable for responsive, secure, timely and cost-effective delivery.
Anticipate dependencies and provider-driven changes, represent BCCF’s needs credibly and secure workable outcomes through collaboration, influence and disciplined follow-up.

4. Technology Risk and Cybersecurity Oversight

Building on BCCF’s current cybersecurity assessment, oversee the operational security measures delivered by PHSA, Blackbaud, and other service providers
Ensure the risks to our technology reliability, and the potential impact of service issues on our business, are understood
Evolve BCCF’s technology risk mitigation approach and our plans to respond to and recover from service disruptions

5. Implementation, Adoption & Future Readiness

Personally lead and coordinate priority technology service improvements and cross-functional implementations, from requirements and vendor coordination through testing, rollout, issue resolution and stabilization.
Partner with the PMO, Data Platforms and Analytics, People and Organization People teams and business owners to manage dependencies, change control, communications, training and adoption so solutions are used effectively.
Maintain a current view of technology capabilities, integrations, licenses, architecture dependencies and replacement horizons; proactively recommend sustainable improvements that reduce complexity and future risk.
Assess emerging technologies and opportunities for secure automation and AI, and translate promising ideas into realistic pilots, business cases, or phased implementation recommendations.

6. Financial Stewardship, Team Leadership & Performance

Manage technology services budgets, assets, software subscriptions and vendor spend with clear forecasting, cost controls and value-for-money decisions.
Lead, coach and develop a small, service-oriented team, clarifying accountability, balancing workloads and building the internal capability needed to manage partners and deliver reliably.
Provide concise reporting to the CSBIO and business leaders on service performance, project delivery, adoption, spend, material risks and decisions required.
Model BCCF’s values — Be Curious, Be Authentic and Be Courageous by embracing innovation, building trusted relationships, communicating transparently, challenging the status quo, proactively addressing risks, and taking ownership of outcomes.

What Success Looks Like

Technology investments and initiatives demonstrate measurable improvements in employee productivity, service effectiveness, technology adoption and organizational value, supported by a realistic, prioritized and financially sustainable roadmap.
Employees and teams can rely on timely, secure and responsive technology support; recurring issues decline, and service satisfaction improves.
PHSA and other providers operate against understood responsibilities, measurable service levels and effective escalation; critical dependencies are proactively managed.
Cybersecurity, privacy, continuity, and third-party risks are visible, assessed and mitigated, with tested plans and no unmanaged critical gaps.

Qualifications

Post-secondary education in technology, information systems, business or an equivalent combination of experience and demonstrated capability.
10+ years of progressive technology experience, including 5+ years leading technology services, teams, vendors or complex delivery.
Proven success leading technology delivery through outsourced, shared-service or SaaS partnerships, with accountability for service performance, contracts and escalations.
Hands-on experience solving operational technology issues, leading implementations and turning business needs into adopted improvements.
Working knowledge of infrastructure, Microsoft 365, identity and access management, enterprise applications, integrations, cybersecurity, privacy and business continuity.
Strong business and financial judgment, including prioritization, business cases, total cost of ownership, vendor negotiations and budget accountability.
Experience with fundraising, CRM or finance systems (e.g., Blackbaud) and healthcare, philanthropy or public-sector partners is an asset.
ITIL, cybersecurity, project or vendor-management credentials are assets but don’t replace proven results.

  Core Competencies

Accountability & Results
— Owns dependable technology service delivery, follows through on commitments, resolves operational issues and delivers measurable service and business improvements.
Collaboration & Influence — Builds trusted relationships across business teams, PHSA and vendors; clarifies needs, negotiates solutions and secures accountability without direct authority.
Judgment & Decision-Making
— Balances reliability, business value, risk, cost and capacity; makes timely, practical decisions, challenges assumptions and escalates material risks with clear recommendations.
Learning, Adaptability, Innovation & Change
— Evaluates emerging technologies, improves existing platforms and leads implementation and adoption through practical change management.
Organizational & Strategic Thinking
— Connects technology investments to BCCF’s 2030 strategy, anticipates future needs and translates direction into achievable roadmaps and priorities.
